passages.text: These men met Zacchaeus while he was staying here and, through him, shared in the word of truth. Having regretted their initial innovations, they quickly condemned Simon. Since they had shared knowledge of everything with him, as soon as I arrived here they approached me together with the woman who had raised them. They were introduced to me by Zacchaeus, and from then on they have always remained with me, benefiting from the teachings of the truth. After Peter said this, he sent for them and ordered them to set out for me precisely everything concerning Simon. They called God as witness that they would tell no lie, and began their account.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Having regretted their initial innovations
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb expresses regret over their earlier innovations; the context does not require the policy term “reorient.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: Since they had shared knowledge of everything with him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The construction can denote being privy to everything together with Simon; “knowing everything about him” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: together with the woman who had raised them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine participle identifies a woman, and the verb denotes bringing up or rearing.

lexical_decisions.chosen: They were introduced to me by Zacchaeus
lexical_decisions.rationale: Zacchaeus is the contextually preferable antecedent of the pronoun, and the verb here denotes presenting or introducing someone.

lexical_decisions.chosen: benefiting from the teachings of the truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle can mean enjoying, partaking of, or benefiting from the instruction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: They called God as witness that they would tell no lie
lexical_decisions.rationale: The construction invokes God as witness to the truthfulness of the account they are about to give.

source_issues.issue: The pronoun can grammatically refer to more than one previously mentioned man. The main text chooses Zacchaeus because he had instructed them locally and could naturally introduce them to Peter; reference to Simon is contextually less likely.

passages.text: Of these, Aquila was the first and began to speak as follows: “Listen, dearest brother, so that you may know precisely everything concerning the man—whose son he is, who he is and where he comes from, what things he does, and how and why. This Simon’s father is Antonius and his mother Rachel. He is a Samaritan by nationality, from Geththon, a village six schoeni from the city. Having been in Alexandria in Egypt, he thoroughly trained himself in Greek learning, became very powerful in magic, and grew conceited. He wants to be regarded as some supreme power, higher even than the God who created the world. At times, while also hinting that he himself is the Messiah, he calls himself ‘the Standing One.’ He uses this designation on the ground that he will always stand and has no cause of decay that would make his body fall. Nor does he say that the God who created the world is supreme. He does not believe that the dead will be raised. He repudiates Jerusalem and advances Mount Gerizim in opposition to it. In place of our actual Messiah, he proclaims himself. He allegorizes the provisions of the Law according to his own preconception. He says that there will be a judgment, but he does not expect it; for if he were convinced that he would be judged by God, he would not have dared to act impiously even against God himself. Consequently, some people, unaware that he uses reverence for God as a veil and stealthily pilfers what belongs to the truth, trustingly believe the hope and judgment which he says will somehow come to pass, and they perish.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίνος τε ὢν καὶ τίς καὶ πόθεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: whose son he is, who he is and where he comes from
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first expression concerns family origin here, as the immediately following identification of Simon’s parents indicates.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a Samaritan by nationality
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase identifies Simon’s ethnic or national affiliation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: from Geththon, a village
lexical_decisions.rationale: “Geththon” directly represents the printed place name; Gitta and Gittha are possible conventional forms.

lexical_decisions.chosen: six schoeni
lexical_decisions.rationale: The schoenus was an ancient unit of variable length, so retaining it avoids an unsupported modern conversion.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ τῇ πρὸς Αἴγυπτον γεγονώς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Having been in Alexandria in Egypt
lexical_decisions.rationale: This preserves the broad force of the expression without deciding whether it denotes residence, presence, or birth; “having been born in Alexandria in Egypt” remains possible.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀνωτάτη τις εἶναι δύναμις καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον κτίσαντος θεοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: some supreme power, higher even than the God who created the world
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive associated with the superlative presents Simon’s claimed power as surpassing even the creator God.

lexical_decisions.chosen: hinting that he himself is the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb denotes suggesting indirectly, while χριστός functions independently as a title.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he calls himself ‘the Standing One’
lexical_decisions.rationale: The perfect participle functions as a designation and begins the section’s repeated standing-and-falling imagery.

lexical_decisions.chosen: advances Mount Gerizim in opposition to it
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb means to bring forward as a counterclaim or substitute; Jerusalem is the contextual point of opposition.

lexical_decisions.chosen: In place of our actual Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle contrasts the real or actual Messiah with Simon’s self-proclamation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ δὲ τοῦ νόμου ἰδίᾳ προλήψει ἀλληγορεῖ
lexical_decisions.chosen: He allegorizes the provisions of the Law according to his own preconception
lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun denotes a prior assumption or preconceived notion governing his allegorical treatment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he uses reverence for God as a veil
lexical_decisions.rationale: Reverence for God is presented as a covering or façade.

lexical_decisions.chosen: trustingly believe
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording preserves the emphatic relationship between the adverb and its cognate verb without adding an unsupported intensifier.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ τῇ πρὸς Αἴγυπτον γεγονώς
source_issues.issue: The participle can describe having been or lived in Alexandria, but it can also denote having been born there. The main wording leaves that distinction open.

source_issues.source_quote: τὰ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ τὴν ὁπώσποτε ὑπὸ αὐτοῦ ἐλπίδα καὶ κρίσιν λεγομένην ἔσεσθαι
source_issues.issue: The syntax is compressed. The hope and judgment may be taken as the fronted object of πιστεύοντες, as in the main text, or included with the things of truth that Simon stealthily appropriates. The placement of ὁπώσποτε also permits either “which he somehow says will occur” or “which he says will somehow occur.”

passages.text: The way he slipped into the doctrine of reverence for God came about as follows: There was a certain John, a daily baptizer, who, according to the principle of pairing, also became the forerunner of our Lord Jesus. Just as our Lord had twelve apostles, bearing the number of the sun’s twelve months, so John too had thirty leading men, fulfilling the moon’s monthly reckoning. Within that number there was one woman named Helena, so that not even this might lie outside the ordered scheme. For the woman, being half a man, made the count of the thirty incomplete, just as the moon’s count is incomplete, since the moon’s journey does not complete its course during the month. Of these thirty, Simon was first and most highly approved by John. The reason he did not assume leadership after John’s death was this:

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ δὲ παρεισελθεῖν αὐτὸν τὸν τῆς θεοσεβείας λόγον
lexical_decisions.chosen: The way he slipped into the doctrine of reverence for God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb suggests intrusive or surreptitious entry, while λόγος here denotes a body of teaching.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a daily baptizer
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound describes one who practices daily baptism; “Hemerobaptist” would be a possible technical transliteration.

lexical_decisions.chosen: according to the principle of pairing
lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun denotes a pairing or paired correspondence within the work’s conceptual scheme.

lexical_decisions.chosen: became the forerunner
lexical_decisions.rationale: The predicate noun concerns going forth or going before and identifies John’s precursor role.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν τοῦ ἡλίου δώδεκα μηνῶν φέροντες τὸν ἀριθμόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: bearing the number of the sun’s twelve months
lexical_decisions.rationale: The source explicitly correlates the twelve apostles with the twelve solar months.

lexical_decisions.chosen: had thirty leading men
lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun denotes chiefs or leading persons. The following sentences explicitly include one woman within this numbered group.

lexical_decisions.chosen: so that not even this might lie outside the ordered scheme
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective describes something unarranged or outside an ordering plan.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἥμισυ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς οὖσα ἡ γυνὴ
lexical_decisions.chosen: For the woman, being half a man
lexical_decisions.rationale: The author’s gendered numerical claim is translated directly without endorsement or mitigation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀτελῆ τὸν τῆς τριακοντάδος τέθεικεν ἀριθμόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: made the count of the thirty incomplete
lexical_decisions.rationale: Within the author’s calculation, Helena’s inclusion produces an incomplete total corresponding to the lunar course.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρῶτος καὶ δοκιμώτατος ἦν ὁ Σίμων
lexical_decisions.chosen: Simon was first and most highly approved
lexical_decisions.rationale: The superlative can mean most approved, esteemed, tested, or qualified.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he did not assume leadership
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb here concerns taking the leading position after John rather than merely beginning an action.

source_issues.source_quote: μία τις ἦν γυνὴ λεγομένη Ἑλένη
source_issues.issue: The source has just described the numbered group as thirty ἄνδρες but then states that one member was a woman. The following explanation deliberately develops this numerical tension, so no correction is warranted.

source_issues.source_quote: τῷ Ἰωάννῃ πρῶτος καὶ δοκιμώτατος ἦν ὁ Σίμων
source_issues.issue: The dative may present Simon as first and most approved in John’s estimation or place him first within the group associated with John. The main text combines rank within the group with John’s approval.

passages.text: For while Simon was away in Egypt to advance his training in magic, John was killed. A certain Dositheus, who coveted the leadership, falsely announced Simon’s death and succeeded to the sect. Simon returned not long afterward and, though he laid strong claim to the position as his own, when he met Dositheus he did not demand it back, knowing that the person who first secures the leadership is not deposed against his will. Therefore, under a pretense of friendship, he submitted himself for a little while to second place under Dositheus. After not many days, once he had been ranked among the thirty fellow disciples, he began secretly to disparage Dositheus, alleging that he was not transmitting the teachings authentically. He said that Dositheus did this not out of envy but out of ignorance. At one point Dositheus perceived that Simon’s artful disparagement was destroying the estimation in which the majority held him, so that he was thought not to be the Standing One. He came in anger to their customary session and, finding Simon, struck him with a staff; but the staff seemed to pass through Simon’s body as though it were smoke. Astonished at this, Dositheus said to him, “If you are the Standing One, then I worship you.” When Simon said, “I am,” Dositheus recognized that he himself was not the Standing One, fell down, and worshiped him. He lowered himself to the level of the twenty-nine chief disciples and installed Simon in the place of esteem that had been his own. And so, after not many days, while Simon stood, Dositheus himself fell and died.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to advance his training in magic
lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun denotes continued practice, training, or cultivation of an ability.

lexical_decisions.chosen: falsely announced Simon’s death
lexical_decisions.rationale: The pronoun most naturally refers to the absent Simon, whose supposed death would remove his claim to succeed John.

lexical_decisions.chosen: succeeded to the sect
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb denotes taking over in succession, while αἵρεσις here refers to the organized school or sect.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ τόπου ὡς ἰδίου μεγάλως ἀντεχόμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: though he laid strong claim to the position as his own
lexical_decisions.rationale: The “place” is the leadership position, and the verb expresses holding firmly to or asserting a claim.

lexical_decisions.chosen: is not deposed against his will
lexical_decisions.rationale: The prepositional phrase is understood as removal contrary to the officeholder’s choice; “regardless of preference” is less likely.

lexical_decisions.chosen: under a pretense of friendship
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression presents friendship as assumed or feigned.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὸν δεύτερον τοῦ Δοσιθέου τόπον δίδωσιν ἑαυτόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: he submitted himself for a little while to second place under Dositheus
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase places Simon in a subordinate, second-ranking position relative to Dositheus.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ταγεὶς δὲ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας τοῖς τριάκοντα συμμαθηταῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: After not many days, once he had been ranked among the thirty fellow disciples
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative is taken as the group to which Simon was assigned, though appointment in relation to or over them is also grammatically possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he began secretly to disparage Dositheus
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound denotes covert or insinuating slander.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς μὴ παραδιδόντα γνησίως τὰ μαθήματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: alleging that he was not transmitting the teachings authentically
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adverb can mean genuinely, faithfully, or authentically.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the estimation in which the majority held him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun is taken as the opinion or supposition about Dositheus among the wider group; “suspicion” is possible lexically but less suitable here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ δὲ ὥσπερ καπνοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος διελθεῖν ἔδοξε σῶμα
lexical_decisions.chosen: but the staff seemed to pass through Simon’s body as though it were smoke
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine pronoun refers back to the staff, while the smoke comparison characterizes Simon’s apparently insubstantial body.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ ἑστώς, καὶ προσκυνῶ σε
lexical_decisions.chosen: If you are the Standing One, then I worship you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The conjunction is taken with apodotic force; “I too worship you” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: He lowered himself to the level of the twenty-nine chief disciples
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle depicts Dositheus lowering himself into the rank associated with the twenty-nine leaders.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ τῆς ὑπονοίας τόπον ἔστησε τὸν Σίμωνα
lexical_decisions.chosen: installed Simon in the place of esteem that had been his own
lexical_decisions.rationale: The unusual phrase is understood as Dositheus’s former place in the group’s estimation; ἔστησε also continues the standing imagery.

lexical_decisions.chosen: while Simon stood, Dositheus himself fell and died
lexical_decisions.rationale: The literal standing-and-falling contrast concludes the wordplay surrounding the designation “the Standing One.”

source_issues.source_quote: ταγεὶς δὲ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας τοῖς τριάκοντα συμμαθηταῖς
source_issues.issue: The dative with the participle permits Simon to be assigned among or to the thirty fellow disciples, or possibly appointed over them. The main rendering chooses ranking among them because the preceding sentence places him second under Dositheus.

source_issues.source_quote: τοῦ μὴ αὐτὸν εἶναι νομίζειν τὸν ἑστῶτα
source_issues.issue: The attachment of the articular infinitive is compressed. It can express the result of Simon’s disparagement—that Dositheus came to be thought not to be the Standing One—or further define the opinion being undone. The main text adopts the result sense.

source_issues.source_quote: Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ ἑστώς, καὶ προσκυνῶ σε
source_issues.issue: The conjunction may introduce the consequence, “then I worship you,” or carry additive force, “I too worship you.” The main text adopts the consequential reading.

The phrase may mean that Dositheus lowered himself to the rank of the twenty-nine chiefs or that he cast himself down together with them. The main rendering chooses the rank relation because he is surrendering his leadership position.

The expression is unusual and may denote Dositheus’s place in public estimation, his supposed status, or the position he believed himself to hold. The main rendering chooses public esteem because the preceding sentence concerns how the majority regarded him.
